text: Training begins with a small, variable number of input face images capturing an individual across diverse poses and expressions.
These images are fed into the Omni-ID Encoder, which integrates individual image features through transformer attention layers.
The encoder outputs the Omni-ID representation, a fixed-size, structured embedding that holistically captures the subject's identity.
This representation is then routed to multiple distinct decoders, combining complementary objectives such as masked autoencoding and flow matching.
Through this few-to-many reconstruction strategy, the decoders generate numerous target facial variations, jointly supervising the encoder.
